items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the town law and the public officers law, in relation to authorizing the town building inspector, town comptroller, accounting officer and clerk of the works of the town of LaGrange in Dutchess County to be nonresidents of the town of LaGrange under certain circumstances
items.lawCode: Amd §23, Town L; amd §3, Pub Off L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7699

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the town law and the public officers
law, in relation to authorizing the town building inspector, town
comptroller, accounting officer and clerk of the works of the town of
LaGrange in Dutchess County to be nonresidents of the town of LaGrange
under certain circumstances

 PURPOSE :

To waive the residency requirements for certain town officer positions
in the town of LaGrange in Dutchess County.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1: Amends Section 23 of the Town Law by adding a new
subdivision to waive the requirement that persons performing the
function of town building inspector, comptroller, accounting officer
and clerk of the works in the town of LaGrange, Dutchess County are
electors of such town.

Section 2: Amends Section 3 of the Public Officers Law by adding a new
subdivision to waive the requirement that persons holding the offices
of town building inspector, comptroller, accounting officer and clerk
of the works in the town of LaGrange, Dutchess County be a resident of
such municipal corporation, provided that said persons resides in
Dutchess County or an adjoining county within New York State.

Section 3: Provides the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

After taking office and reviewing town laws, the town of LaGrange
Supervisor noticed that several of the town officer positions would be
considered non-compliant due to residency requirements. Through a
resolution, the town has expressed their desire to allow all three
members to continue to perform their respective duties as town
officers due to their experience and deep town knowledge and do not
wish to replace them. Each of these town officers have been in their
position for at least eight years, and this bill would give the town
the ability to keep them on in their current positions without being
considered non-compliant.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the state.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
